client_alerts.headline: GitHub Copilot can now drive desktop applications — a new path to client data on developer machines
client_alerts.body: GitHub put **computer use** into public preview on Oct 1 for the Copilot CLI and the Copilot app on macOS and Windows. Copilot can now operate GUI-only and legacy software that has no API, CLI or MCP integration. For clients with Copilot Business or Enterprise, ask whether preview features are enabled by policy, which machines hold production consoles or regulated data, and whether screen content handled by the agent is covered by existing DLP and logging.

client_alerts.headline: Microsoft 365 Copilot: Cowork, Code and Autopilot entry points become visible by default this month
client_alerts.body: Per Microsoft's September update, the **Cowork, Code and Autopilot** entry points show to licensed users by default starting in **October for standard-release tenants** and **November for deferred tenants**. Clients who have not reviewed agent settings will see these appear without an admin decision. Have tenant admins confirm the intended state and the cost-management limits (Copilot Studio agents are added to cost management in October) before users find them.

top_moves.title: GitHub Copilot adds desktop computer use and code-defined multi-agent workflows
top_moves.body: Computer use is in public preview in the Copilot CLI and Copilot app on macOS and Windows, and **dynamic workflows** let teams define an orchestration in code across the CLI, app and SDK. Upfront charges for Copilot Business and Enterprise seats paid by card or PayPal also began Oct 1.

top_moves.title: Anthropic ships mods for Claude Code
top_moves.body: **Mods** are small TypeScript functions that rewrite prompts, add UI or replace built-in features in the Claude Code CLI and desktop app; they ship inside plugins and arrived with Claude Code 2.1.287. Separately, Anthropic's Sept 30 notes list **Claude Sonnet 4.5 retiring Nov 30** and Claude for Government reaching general availability with FedRAMP High.

top_moves.title: Microsoft 365 Copilot's October wave starts: agent entry points on by default, 'Today' in private preview
top_moves.body: Cowork, Code and Autopilot entry points become visible by default for standard-release tenants this month. Also rolling out in October: a proactive **Today** view (private preview), PowerPoint Skills for brand managers, and PowerPoint tasks that keep running after the user leaves.

providers.name: OpenAI
providers.headline: Post-DevDay follow-ups: Codex 0.160.0 today, plus consumer shopping features and an Albertsons partnership on Oct 1
providers.detail: Codex 0.160.0 (Oct 2) adds history browsing in the agent command center, projectless sessions with workspace defaults and Guardian review improvements. On Oct 1 ChatGPT added virtual try-on, product Favorites and multi-page document scanning to PDF on iOS, and OpenAI announced a Safeway shopping experience with Albertsons. Nothing today changes the DevDay picture reported yesterday (Dots, GPT-6.1 Sol at $2/$10 per million tokens, Pro 500).

providers.name: Anthropic
providers.headline: Claude Code gets mods — TypeScript functions that change or extend the CLI and desktop app
providers.detail: Mods (Oct 1) can rewrite a prompt, add UI, replace a built-in feature or add new functionality, and are distributed inside plugins; Claude Code 2.1.287 carries the support along with plugin, MCP, accessibility and Windows fixes. The Sept 30 notes also list Claude for Government as generally available with FedRAMP High authorization, and **Claude Sonnet 4.5 deprecated with retirement on Nov 30, 2026**. Anything pinned to Sonnet 4.5 needs a migration target before then.

providers.name: Google Gemini
providers.headline: Gemini 4 Argon remains a restricted preview for cyber defenders; no wider access date yet
providers.detail: No new release today. Google's Sept 30 post has Gemini 4 Argon rolling out only to trusted cyber defenders through the Fairwind Program, with paid API and Google AI Ultra access to follow 'as soon as possible'. Stated terms: 1M-token output, introductory pricing of $2 input / $10 output per million tokens, rising to $4 / $20 afterwards.

providers.name: xAI
providers.headline: Musk announces major Grok speed improvements on Oct 1, with no benchmarks published
providers.detail: The Oct 1 announcement claims a large speed gain following the Sept 21 Grok 4.7 launch, but no figures were shared, so treat it as unverified. Grok 4.7 is also listed as available on Google's Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform. Grok 5 is still in training with no date.

providers.detail: No new Meta AI release or policy change turned up in today's searches.

providers.headline: Quiet today; the enterprise Le Chat → Vibe migration window that opened Oct 1 is the live item
providers.detail: No new release. Enterprise administrators choose when to migrate to the new Vibe experience within a roughly six-month window that opened Oct 1, as reported yesterday.

providers.name: Perplexity
providers.headline: Quiet today; latest published release notes are still the Sept 21 Effort Mode update
providers.detail: No new Perplexity release notes since Sept 21 (Effort Mode, GPT-6 Astra, Skills Marketplace, Portable and Hybrid Computer).

providers.name: Microsoft 365 Copilot
providers.headline: October wave begins: Copilot Cowork, Code and Autopilot entry points visible by default for standard-release tenants
providers.detail: The Cowork, Code and Autopilot entry points become visible to licensed users by default this month for standard-release tenants; deferred-release tenants follow in November. Also slated for October: the proactive **Today** view across mail, calendar, chats and tasks (private preview, then Outlook and Teams), PowerPoint Skills for brand managers, PowerPoint tasks that continue after the user leaves or goes offline, an upgraded Copilot new-tab page in Edge, and Copilot Studio agents added to cost management.
providers.alertReason: Agent entry points become visible to licensed users by default in October (standard) and November (deferred).

providers.name: GitHub Copilot
providers.headline: Computer use enters public preview in the Copilot CLI and app; dynamic workflows ship; upfront seat billing starts
providers.detail: All three landed Oct 1. Computer use lets Copilot operate desktop applications on macOS and Windows, including GUI-only and legacy software. Dynamic workflows define multi-agent orchestration in code across the CLI, app and SDK. The VS Code September roll-up adds scheduled recurring work and agent merge for pull requests. Upfront charges now apply to existing Copilot Business and Enterprise customers paying by card or PayPal.
providers.alertReason: Computer use gives the agent access to whatever is on screen in desktop applications.

providers.detail: No Gamma product update found in today's searches.

providers.name: Notion AI
providers.headline: Notion's JavaScript SDK v5.27.0 blocks browser-side tokens by default and adds an Agent Skills API
providers.detail: Released Sept 29 and not previously covered here. Creating an authenticated client in a browser, web worker or service worker now throws an error unless explicitly overridden, which closes a common token-leak mistake. New client.plugins and client.skills methods return signed archive URLs. A third-party pricing write-up also reports per-run credits for workers on Business and Enterprise from Oct 15; that is not confirmed in Notion's own release notes.
